tools.name: get_vault_overview
tools.description: Read the whole vault catalog in one call: every layer with its techs (kind, use_when, avoid_when, performs_best), the stack profiles and the past projects. Archived projects are omitted; finished (done) projects stay, so their stack and lessons still inform the next choice. Use it to reason over the vault when a ranked shortlist is not enough; read deciding notes with get_note before choosing. Read-only.

layers.description: Restrict the catalog to these layer ids

tools.name: list_layers
tools.description: List the stack layers (backend, frontend, testing, ...) and the technologies stored under each.

tools.name: search_vault
tools.description: Full-text search over the user's stack vault. Returns ranked hits (id, type, title, score) plus the total that matched, so a capped list says so. Use before proposing new notes to avoid duplicates.

layer.description: Restrict to tech notes in this layer

tools.name: get_note
tools.description: Read a vault note (frontmatter + markdown body) plus which notes link to it.

tools.name: recommend_stack
tools.description: Given a natural-language project description, return ranked technology candidates per layer and matching stack profiles from the user's vault. Each candidate carries the `use_when`/`performs_best`/`avoid_when` phrases that matched and the `score_breakdown` parts that scored (weighted keyword overlap scaled by word rarity, plus negation and language fit; `hybrid` when embeddings are on). `per_layer` is a maximum, not a minimum: a layer with nothing above zero is omitted. Treat it as a shortlist: read the candidate notes, choose, and explain the choice to the user. Prefer the user's vault over general knowledge.

tools.name: get_stack_context
tools.description: Compile best practices and validation checks for a chosen set of technologies into one markdown document. Call once the stack is chosen and follow it while writing code; run the listed checks before declaring work done.

tools.name: get_check_templates
tools.description: Return the file templates (tests, configs) shipped by the checks of a chosen stack. Write missing files into the project; never overwrite existing files.

tools.name: detect_stack
tools.description: Detect technologies and versions from a project directory's package.json, pyproject.toml and requirements files. Read-only.

tools.name: propose_note
tools.description: Propose a new note or an update to an existing one. It lands in the vault inbox for the user to approve; it is NOT applied directly. Frontmatter must match the note type schema (e.g. tech: kind, layer, use_when, avoid_when, performs_best, practices, checks). Use [[id]] wikilinks in the body to connect notes.

frontmatter.description: Fields for the note type, excluding 'type'

reason.description: Why this note should be added/changed

agent.description: Name of the proposing agent, e.g. 'claude-code'

tools.name: record_project_outcome
tools.description: Propose an outcome for a project note: append lessons, optionally extend tech notes (use_when, avoid_when, performs_best, lessons) and add a dated outcome section. A finished (done) project still accepts outcomes: its lessons keep counting for later decisions. Everything lands in the vault inbox for review; nothing is applied directly.

summary.description: What happened and what was learned

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Render the files that make a project's coding agents follow the user's stack: STACK.md always, plus AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and/or Cursor rules. Pass the current file contents in `existing` so agent-file blocks merge instead of overwriting user text; basics never writes outside the vault.

existing.description: Current file contents keyed by relative path

tools.name: list_proposals
tools.description: List agent proposals waiting for user review in the vault inbox.

prompts.name: plan-stack
prompts.description: Plan a project's stack from the vault: read the whole catalog and the ranked shortlist, decide one tech per layer, explain the choice, propose any note the vault is missing for that decision and ask for confirmation before writing files.

arguments.name: project
arguments.description: What the user is building: product, users and any constraint already known.

contract.prompt:
Plan the stack for this project:

Counter dashboard

Work from the user's vault, not from general knowledge:

1. `get_vault_overview` for every layer with its techs (`use_when`, `avoid_when`, `performs_best`), the profiles and the past projects. Pass `layers` only when the user already named them.
2. `recommend_stack` with the same description as a cross-check. It is a shortlist, not the decision.
3. `get_note` on the deciding notes before committing, especially when two candidates are close or a profile looks like a match.

Answer with a short **stack decision**: one tech per needed layer, one line of reason each citing the vault note (`[[id]]`) and the `use_when` it matched; name any `avoid_when` that ruled out an alternative. Prefer a matching profile, and what past projects used successfully while respecting their lessons.

Fill the gaps the decision exposes: when a tech it needs has no note, or a chosen note links a missing `[[id]]`, `search_vault` then `propose_note` — never more notes than the decision uses. Each proposal needs the right `type`; for a tech its `kind`, `layer` (an existing layer id) and `language` when it applies; at least 2 `use_when`, 1 `avoid_when`, `tags` and `related`; `[[id]]` links and `related` only to notes that exist or that you propose now; a 3–6 line body (what it is, when it beats the alternatives in the vault, one pitfall); and a `reason` naming the decision that needed it.

List the proposals ("Propuestas al Inbox: rustls, reqwest") and repeat that nothing is applied until the user approves it in the Inbox. Then ask ONE question: "¿Usamos este stack? / Shall we use this stack?" in the user's language.

After a yes, follow the skill's New project steps: `get_stack_context` for the chosen techs, `get_check_templates` for the files to create, then `export_project` (send the existing agent file contents in `existing`) and write the returned files into the project root.

# Stack context

## Technologies

### React (`react`)

- layer: frontend
- use when: SPA interactiva tipo dashboard o panel; interfaz con mucho estado de cliente
- avoid when: sitio estático de contenido casi sin interactividad

#### React

Librería de UI. Para SSR/SEO usar [[nextjs]].

### TypeScript (`typescript`)

- layer: frontend, backend
- use when: aplicaciones web frontend; backend Node compartiendo tipos con frontend; herramientas CLI y servidores MCP
- avoid when: computación numérica intensiva

#### TypeScript

Base de [[react]] y [[nextjs]]. Tests con [[vitest]].

### Playwright (`playwright`)

- layer: testing
- use when: tests end-to-end de aplicaciones web en navegador; validar flujos de usuario críticos como login o checkout
- avoid when: lógica pura sin interfaz

#### Playwright

Tests E2E de navegador.


## Best practices

### Componentes React (`react-components`)

- Componentes pequeños y puros; estado lo más cerca de donde se usa.
- Estado de servidor con TanStack Query (o server components en [[nextjs]]), no en `useState`.
- Accesibilidad: elementos semánticos, labels en inputs, navegable con teclado.

### TypeScript estricto (`typescript-strict`)

- `"strict": true` en tsconfig; prohibido `any` implícito.
- Validar datos externos en el borde con `zod`, derivar tipos con `z.infer`.
- Preferir uniones discriminadas sobre flags booleanos.


## Checks (validate generated code against these)

### Typecheck TypeScript (`typescript-typecheck`)

- kind: build
- run: `npx tsc --noEmit`

Cero errores de tipo. No silenciar con `@ts-ignore` sin comentario justificando.

### Flujos críticos E2E (`e2e-critical-flows`)

- kind: test
- run: `npx playwright test`

Cada flujo crítico (registro, login, acción principal del producto) tiene un test E2E que pasa en Chromium y Firefox.
Usar selectores por rol (`getByRole`), no por clases CSS.

skillBody:
If the `basics` tools are not available, tell the user to connect the server (`claude mcp add --transport http basics
http://127.0.0.1:4747/mcp` while `basics ui` or the desktop app is running) and stop; do not imitate the tools.

## Rules

- **The vault beats general knowledge.** When a vault note covers a decision, follow it. If you disagree, say so and
  explain why, but do not silently pick something else.
- **Nothing is applied directly.** `propose_note` and `record_project_outcome` put proposals in the vault inbox for the
  user to review. Say "proposed for review", never "added" or "saved".
- **Never overwrite project files.** Templates and exported files are written only where no file exists yet, except the
  marked `<!-- basics:start -->` … `<!-- basics:end -->` blocks that `export_project` merges.
- **Search before you propose.** Run `search_vault` first so you update an existing note instead of creating a
  duplicate.
- Pass your client name as `agent` (for example `claude-code`). Names starting with `pack:` are reserved.

## New project

If the client supports MCP prompts, start with the `plan-stack` prompt and the project description: it runs the
whole flow below in one step. Otherwise follow these steps.

1. `get_vault_overview` for the whole catalog (layers, techs, profiles and past projects) and `recommend_stack` with
   the project description as a ranked cross-check. Treat the ranking as a shortlist, not the decision.
2. Decide yourself from the vault: one tech per needed layer. Prefer a matching profile when one fits. Prefer what
   past projects used successfully, and respect their lessons. If the decision needs something the vault does not
   have yet, fill the gap (see [Filling gaps](#filling-gaps)).
3. Tell the user the decision in this shape, one line per layer:

   `Vamos a usar: <layer>: <tech> — <reason from [[note]]>`

   Then list the alternatives you ruled out and why (from their `avoid_when`), and list any proposals you made
   ("Propuestas al Inbox: rustls, reqwest") saying nothing is applied until the user approves it. Ask ONE question —
   "¿Usamos este stack? / Shall we use this stack?" — before writing any file.
4. After the user says yes, `get_stack_context` with the chosen tech ids. Keep that document as your working rules for
   the project.
5. `get_check_templates` and write the files that do not exist yet.
6. `export_project` with the stack. Send the current contents of `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or Cursor rules in `existing`
   so the user's own text survives, then write the returned files into the project root.
7. If the project has no project note, `propose_note` with type `project`, the stack by layer and the description.
   Say "proposed for review"; it lands in the vault inbox.

## Filling gaps

Sometimes the right decision uses a technology the vault has no note for, or a chosen note links to a `[[id]]` that
was never written. Close that gap with a proposal instead of quietly falling back on general knowledge.

1. `search_vault` for the missing note, then `get_note` on the closest hits: if a note already covers it, propose an
   update instead of a duplicate.
2. `propose_note` only the notes the decision actually uses — never a wish list.
3. Make each proposal useful on its own: correct `type`, and for a tech the right `kind` and `layer` (an existing
   layer id) plus `language` when it applies; at least 2 `use_when`, at least 1 `avoid_when`, `tags` and `related`.
   Link `[[id]]` in the body and `related` only to notes that exist or that you propose in the same answer. Write a
   body of 3–6 lines, specific: what it is, when it beats the alternatives already in the vault, and one concrete
   pitfall or setup note. The `reason` says which project decision needed it.
4. List the proposals in your answer ("Propuestas al Inbox: rustls, reqwest") and say they are proposed for review:
   nothing is applied until the user approves it in the Inbox.

## Existing project

1. If the project has `STACK.md`, read it: it is the compiled context. If it has `basics.json`, its `stack` lists the
   tech ids.
2. Otherwise run `detect_stack` on the project directory and confirm the detected technologies with the user.
3. `get_stack_context` with those ids (and `versions` from `basics.json` or `detect_stack`) before you change code.

## While coding

- Follow the practices in the stack context. When a practice conflicts with what the user asks, point it out and let
  them decide.
- Before you say the work is done, run the checks listed in the stack context and report each result. A failing check
  means the work is not done.

## Teaching the vault

- When you learn something worth keeping (a pitfall, a version quirk, a better default), `search_vault` for the note,
  then `propose_note` with the full frontmatter and body and a one-line `reason`. Link related notes with `[[id]]`.
- At the end of meaningful work on a project, `record_project_outcome` with a short summary, the lessons and any
  `tech_updates`. The project id is the `project` field in `basics.json`; if there is no project note, propose one with
  `propose_note` (type `project`) first.
- `list_proposals` shows what is still waiting for review; do not propose the same change twice.
